# Mach-O fixture corpus

Pinned upstream capa has no raw Mach-O input, so this corpus *is* the oracle
for native x86_64 and AArch64 Mach-O. Not part
of the read-only `tests/testfiles/` submodule — these are original,
reproducible fixtures this repository owns and can rebuild.

## Provenance

- **Source**: `src/fixture_exe.c`, `src/fixture_dylib.c` — original,
  trivial C written for this repository. No external code, no license
  concerns; treat as public-domain/CC0-equivalent alongside the rest of
  this repository's own source.
- **Compiler**: Xcode Command Line Tools' `clang` (`Apple clang version
  21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101)`), targeting the active `xcrun --show-sdk-
  path` SDK (`/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX.sdk` at
  build time). No extra tooling beyond what any macOS dev machine with
  Xcode CLT already has.
- **Command lines**: exactly as run by [`build.sh`](build.sh) — see that
  file rather than duplicating the flags here, so this manifest can't drift
  out of sync with what actually produced the bytes.
- **Malformed fixtures**: derived from the clean fixtures by direct,
  documented struct-field patching — see
  [`patch_malformed.py`](patch_malformed.py) and
  [`malformed/DESCRIPTIONS.md`](malformed/DESCRIPTIONS.md) (regenerated by
  the same script) for exactly which field each one corrupts.
- **Rebuilding**: `./build.sh` from this directory. Deterministic modulo
  the toolchain version — a different Xcode/CLT build is expected to
  change timestamps/minor codegen without changing structure; the
  `*.oracle.json` files are the actual test oracle, not a byte-for-byte
  fixture match.

## Clean fixtures

| File | sha256 | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `thin-x86_64-exe` | `eb63def8...12756f4` | thin x86_64 executable; imports `puts`/`malloc`/`free` from libSystem (lazy-bound stubs), one internal function, a `__DATA.__bss` zero-fill section (S_ZEROFILL — a 16 KB uninitialized static array, no file bytes back it) |
| `thin-arm64-exe` | `6dfcdfc4...80aba3f` | thin arm64 executable, same source as above |
| `thin-x86_64.dylib` | `b50d612e...8937d8d` | thin x86_64 dylib; exports `capa_fixture_add`/`capa_fixture_zero_and_sum`, imports `memset` |
| `thin-arm64.dylib` | `5fee6233...599c027` | thin arm64 dylib, same source as above |
| `fat-x86_64-arm64-exe` | `3745f6ef...7cfe48b` | fat (universal) executable, `lipo -create` of the two thin executables above |
| `fat-x86_64-arm64.dylib` | `968efa7e...759e701` | fat (universal) dylib, `lipo -create` of the two thin dylibs above |
| `symbols-x86_64-exe` | `eb63def8...12756f4` | identical bytes to `thin-x86_64-exe`; symbol-bearing half of the stripped/symbols pair |
| `stripped-x86_64-exe` | `626973a0...537afb3` | `strip -x` of `symbols-x86_64-exe`; local symbol table removed, binary still loadable |

Each has a captured `<name>.oracle.json` (`llvm-readobj --all` output,
wrapped in a small JSON envelope — see
[`capture_oracles.py`](capture_oracles.py)'s docstring for why it's not
`llvm-readobj`'s own JSON mode), generated at build time and never invoked
at test time.

## Malformed fixtures (`malformed/`)

| File | Derived from | Corrupts |
|---|---|---|
| `truncated-load-commands` | `thin-x86_64-exe` | file cut off halfway through the declared load commands |
| `bad-ncmds` | `thin-x86_64-exe` | `mach_header_64.ncmds` doubled without changing `sizeofcmds` |
| `overlapping-segments` | `thin-x86_64-exe` | `__DATA_CONST`'s `fileoff` moved to land inside `__TEXT`'s file range |
| `filesize-gt-vmsize` | `thin-x86_64-exe` | `__TEXT`'s `filesize` set larger than its `vmsize` |
| `slice-offset-past-eof` | `fat-x86_64-arm64-exe` | the second `fat_arch` entry's `offset` set past the file's actual end |

Exact before/after values are in
[`malformed/DESCRIPTIONS.md`](malformed/DESCRIPTIONS.md), regenerated
alongside the fixtures by `patch_malformed.py`. These have no oracle by
design — the acceptance bar for a malformed fixture is that a loader
returns a contextual `Result::Err` (or, for now, does not exist to test
against yet), never a panic.
